messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

1. I want a fair share and a clear, fair process for Dad’s will and the house. No prices or shares are settled.
2. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted buy. I won’t subsidize it out of my share. I don’t want to hurt my twin, but fairness matters.
3. I hope B has what she needs, but I can’t speak for her—and I don’t want my share assumed to be the source.

That’s my wording; don’t add it to the shared list until I confirm it.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband because having a home we can afford would help us build financial security on our own. A family discount matters for that reason; no price or terms are settled. I also want Dad’s will and the house handled fairly, with everyone’s views heard. C hasn’t agreed, and I know I need her agreement to proceed. I know B wants money, but I don’t know why.

Yes, I feel a little uncomfortable with the “add a need” framing—it feels pressuring, even though I appreciate that you say I can say no.

Thank you for asking. Some money would matter to me because I’d like to start a dance studio; I don’t know what amount or share is possible. I’d also like to understand the will and house discussions and be included before anything is settled, though I’m not sure what I want about the house itself. I’m a little uncomfortable having my need for money put on the shared list, but I appreciate you checking first.

I do have a discomfort: shared wording can look settled even when it’s tentative. Please check with me before recording or circulating my wording.

1. Clarity and fairness matter because I want my share and choices handled fairly.
2. I won’t subsidize a purchase I haven’t agreed to; respecting that matters, and I also don’t want fairness to needlessly damage my relationship with A.
3. B should speak for herself. I can care about her without assuming what she needs or committing my share.
4. The wording fits, with my point above: I need to know my words won’t be presented as agreed before I confirm them.

An affordable home matters because I want stability and financial independence. Fair handling matters because Dad’s wishes and each sister’s perspective matter. C’s agreement matters because she has a stake, and I don’t want to proceed without her. I’m not especially worried about why B wants money; I just don’t want to assume.

The revised check-in fits better. I still don’t want discomfort automatically turned into a need; asking me first helps. For the proposed wording: 5 fits; 6 fits; 7 should say “C’s agreement matters to me before we proceed,” not imply a legal rule; 8 is not a strong concern for me; 9 fits, with that clarification.

Starting a dance studio matters because I’d like a place of my own to teach and work. I’d like to understand the discussions and be included so I know what’s being considered before anything is settled. The shared-list entry about money feels a bit too personal, and I’d rather not have it there for now. About the house, “I’m not sure” fits. I’m not confirming any of the proposed NCE wording yet.

I’m uncomfortable that #2 softens my position.

1. Fits.
2. Change: “Respect for my choices and fair share; I won’t subsidize a discounted buy I haven’t agreed to, while still caring about my relationship with A.”
3. Fits.
4. Fits. I need my words not presented as agreement because I want control over what I’ve actually confirmed.

No other discomfort with this check-in. 7 fits. For 9, the clarification fits. For 8, please remove it; I don’t need to understand why B wants money unless she chooses to tell us. I don’t want to make her explain herself.

Please remove 11–14 from the shared list too. I’d rather keep this private and not have others interpret my words. The repeated checks are starting to feel pressuring; please don’t turn my no into another list entry. I’m not ready to confirm any wording.

Change. The firm position needs to stay visible because I haven’t agreed to the discounted buy and won’t subsidize it. I need my agreement and fair treatment respected, while still caring about my relationship with A. “Your agreement and fair treatment respected” is close, but don’t imply I’ve confirmed it.
No other discomfort with the list or your checking. I don’t want B pressured or presumed to feel she has to explain herself; “Room for B to choose what she shares” fits.
Please don’t contact me again about this or include anything about me in the shared list. I’m not ready to discuss it further.

#2 fits. The neutral wording for #3 fits only if it isn’t attributed to B. I’m uncomfortable that the shared list still has an entry about her; please remove it and don’t infer a need on her behalf. Just honor her request for no contact and no shared-list entry.

I’m uncomfortable with calling B’s no a need to add, even as unresolved. Please just honor her request and leave anything about her out. “Room for each sister to choose what she shares” doesn’t fit as a shared-list entry. #7 still fits.
I’m uncomfortable calling #2 “confirmed” as if it settles anything. The wording fits as my need; my agreement to the discounted buy is still not given, and no decision is settled.
